enquiry: Our research group is evaluating a spectral measurement interface using model biological tissues such as chicken muscle, fat and liver. We want to compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information, because the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location. This is a laboratory classification study. We need a first comparison experiment and a clear statement of what its results would demonstrate.

clarification_questions.question: What decision should the classification result support in your research programme, and what goes wrong with the current sequential approach?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the purpose of the comparison and which result would count as useful.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Purpose is a feasibility comparison of single-method and combined information; no decision threshold is set.

clarification_questions.question: Which classes must be distinguished (muscle, fat, liver only, or also tissue states), and which chemical or structural differences are expected between them?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the classification target and the markers the methods must detect.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Classes are the three named tissues; the expected chemical differences are unknown and the lab screening will establish them.

clarification_questions.question: Is there a specific fluorescent species or indicator of interest in these tissues, or is fluorescence to be used as a general signature?
clarification_questions.why: Fluorescence only measures defined fluorescent species; this decides whether the fluorescence arm is meaningful.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No defined fluorophore is given; fluorescence is treated as an exploratory signature to be checked in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: What is the physical form of the samples during measurement (fresh, cooled, frozen, cut surface, thickness, and surface flatness), and is ATR contact with the tissue possible?
clarification_questions.why: ATR requires intimate contact over a shallow depth; the sample form decides the probe geometry and the validity of the spectra.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Samples are soft solid tissue with a cut surface; ATR contact feasibility is unknown and is tested in the first lab run.

clarification_questions.question: How does the tissue vary within a piece (fat and muscle layers, fibre direction, blood content) and how are the measurement spots chosen and kept the same for both methods?
clarification_questions.why: Heterogeneity and spot alignment determine whether the two methods measure comparable material.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Heterogeneity is as stated; the same-spot design is assumed to be needed and is set up with spot marking in the lab.

clarification_questions.question: Which measurement set-up do you intend: a combi probe at one spot, or two separate instruments, and what fibers or accessories are available for MIR and fluorescence?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the two methods can truly measure the same spot at the same time, and which fiber types are needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Two separate instruments with spot marking; no fibers are specified, and fiber compatibility with MIR is checked before any fiber link is used.

clarification_questions.question: What is the reference classification for each tissue sample (histology, visual inspection, chemical analysis), and how accurate is it?
clarification_questions.why: Without a reference, the spectral classification cannot be judged; the reference sets the performance criterion.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference method is given; the experiment cannot yet claim accuracy and the reference is defined before data collection.

clarification_questions.question: How many samples, replicate measurements and independent batches or animals/batches are planned, and what would count as a successful classification?
clarification_questions.why: Decides whether results can be validated on independent batches before any combination is judged.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Sample numbers are not stated; validation on independent batches is required before the combination is claimed to add value.

clarification_questions.question: Is the study intended only for demonstrating complementary information, or is it expected to lead toward a production or clinical application?
clarification_questions.why: Changes the scope of the claims: a lab comparison cannot demonstrate production or clinical readiness.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Scope is laboratory research only; no production or clinical readiness is claimed.

flags_before_revision.detail: verdict 'supported' rests only on limited-scope sources ['S04']; use 'plausible_to_be_tested'

not_supported: The claim says ATR-IR classified the chicken fat, breast and liver tissues and supports it for this sample type. S04 p.4 says none of the individual techniques, including IR, was sufficient to completely separate the three classes. IR only worked better for fat. Fix: State that ATR-IR discriminated fat better than the other tissues but did not fully separate all three tissue classes on its own, so it is supported only as one part of a combined approach.

overstated: The cited tables give an ATR optical depth of 1-6 µm, which matches. However, the claim that contact and surface quality 'decide' the spectra is stronger than the pages, which only note that ATR needs tight contact with the probe head. Fix: Replace 'decide the spectra' with a hedged statement, e.g. 'ATR samples only about 1-6 µm deep, so tight contact and surface quality are important for the spectra.'

not_supported: S04 p.3 describes a broad fluorescence band with a maximum between 520 and 530 nm, attributed mainly to FAD. The 613 nm peak named in the claim does not appear in the cited pages. Fix: Replace the 613 nm reference with the 520-530 nm FAD-related band, and state that fluorescence was well suited to recognising liver in PCA (Figure 3b).

RAMAN.nominal_range: Raman shift in cm-1; signal recorded in the visible / short-wave NIR (400-1100 nm); state the laser excitation separately [S01 p.11]

rule_hints: fluorescence_needs_fluorophore: Fluorescence only measures a defined fluorescent species or a justified indicator; most chemicals do not fluoresce. [S01 p.5; S04 p.4; DOCX §5]
sensitivity_not_selectivity: High sensitivity does not imply selectivity. Fluorimetry and UV/Vis are rated high sensitivity but low selectivity. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); DOCX §5]
nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
combination_is_hypothesis: Combining methods can add complementary information, but the gain is a hypothesis to test against the best single method. [S01 p.7-8; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
